brief.headline: Apollo trades more than $35bn of private credit
bullets: Private Credit: Apollo Global Management has traded more than $35bn of private credit since launching a market-making operation for the asset class, according to a report by Bloomberg citing comments made by the firm's co-head of corporate credit John Cortese.
Fed & Rates: Bridgewater founder Ray Dalio warns that China and Japan may reduce their demand for US government debt, potentially increasing pressure on Treasury yields and federal borrowing costs.

Fed & Rates: Federal Reserve official Waller spoke on “The Signaling Value of the Summary of Economic Projections” at the Istanbul Economic Forum, Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye, Istanbul, Türkiye.

Investor Outlook: Many client questions I received last week in California were laden with a sense of foreboding: third rail questions about the US Federal debt as ten year yields blow through the Bessent Maginot line, the elevated share of US market returns and growth attributable to AI.

Infrastructure & Energy: German utilities company RWE has sought to play down expectations of it playing a significant role in Uniper if its joint bid with KKR for the state-owned energy company succeeds, according to a report by Bloomberg.
brief.marketRead: The S&P 500 stands at 7,801.77 (down 0.2% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 15.1, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.27% (down 4 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.51 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.09%, near long-run norms (up 6 bps on the prior reading). Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits.

items.title: Apollo trades more than $35bn of private credit
items.takeaway: Apollo Global Management has traded more than $35bn of private credit since launching a market-making operation for the asset class, according to a report by Bloomberg citing comments made by the firm's co-head of corporate credit John Cortese.
items.whyItMatters: Apollo is a private-credit heavyweight whose insurance arm, Athene, supplies long-term capital, which makes it central to the fusion of insurance and private lending. Developments here show how easily companies can borrow outside the banking system, and at what price. For allocators: private credit offers high floating-rate income but less liquidity, so manager selection and underwriting discipline matter.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.09%, near long-run norms (up 6 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 7.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.

items.title: RWE downplays Uniper role after joint bid with KKR
items.takeaway: German utilities company RWE has sought to play down expectations of it playing a significant role in Uniper if its joint bid with KKR for the state-owned energy company succeeds, according to a report by Bloomberg.
items.whyItMatters: KKR pioneered the leveraged buyout and now spans private equity, infrastructure, credit and insurance, so its activity is a barometer for global dealmaking. Demand for power, data centers and energy transition projects is pulling record private capital into infrastructure. For allocators: infrastructure can diversify a portfolio, but deal sizes are large and access often runs through the biggest managers.
